aaaa.definition: DNS record mapping a name to an IPv6 address ("quad-A").

accessPointAP.definition: A wireless device that bridges Wi-Fi clients onto a wired LAN.

ack.definition: Fourth DHCPv4 message: server commits the lease.

apiToken.definition: Bearer token gating the NIAC daemon’s REST API. Set via NIAC_API_TOKEN environment variable.

aRecord.definition: DNS record mapping a name to an IPv4 address.

arp.definition: Address Resolution Protocol (RFC 826). Maps IPv4 addresses to MAC addresses on a local Ethernet link.

authoritativeServer.definition: A DNS server that holds the actual records for a zone. NIAC IS one of these (for configured zones).

bpdu.definition: Bridge Protocol Data Unit — the frames exchanged by STP to negotiate a loop-free topology.

bpf.definition: A Berkeley Packet Filter (BPF) expression applied by the capture engine. Packets that don't match are dropped before capture — they never reach the buffer, unlike a display filter.

bridge.definition: A device that forwards frames between two or more LAN segments at Layer 2. Switches are multi-port bridges.

broadcastDomain.definition: The set of devices that receive each other’s broadcast frames. A VLAN defines a broadcast domain.

capabilityTLV.definition: In LLDP/CDP, a TLV announcing what the device is (router, bridge, AP, station-only).

captureBuffer.definition: The daemon’s in-memory rolling pcap. Use `niac dump` to flush it to disk.

cdp.definition: Cisco Discovery Protocol. Cisco’s proprietary L2 discovery protocol; emits frames every 60s announcing device identity, capabilities, and platform.

chassisID.definition: In LLDP, a unique identifier for the device chassis — usually its MAC address.

communityString.definition: The shared secret used to authenticate SNMPv1/v2c requests. "public" is the historical default and is insecure.

daemonMode.definition: NIAC running long-lived, with the embedded web UI active. Started with `niac daemon`.

defaultGateway.definition: The router an end-host sends off-subnet traffic to.

deviceSimulator.definition: NIAC, in one phrase — a tool that pretends to be one or more network devices on a real interface.

dhcp.definition: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (RFC 2131). Hands out IP addresses, gateways, DNS servers, and other network parameters to clients.

dhcpv6.definition: IPv6 variant of DHCP (RFC 8415). Two modes: stateful (assigns addresses) and stateless (options-only, complementing SLAAC).

discover.definition: First DHCPv4 message: client broadcasts "I need an IP." Followed by OFFER, REQUEST, ACK.

dns.definition: Domain Name System (RFC 1035). Translates names to IPs (A, AAAA records) and reverse (PTR).

draft.definition: A saved, editable simulation configuration. Editing a draft does not change the running simulation; review and start it when it is ready.

edp.definition: Extreme Discovery Protocol — Extreme Networks’ proprietary L2 discovery, pre-dating LLDP.

eui64.definition: A method to generate a 64-bit interface ID from a 48-bit MAC, used to autoconfigure IPv6 link-local addresses.

faultInjection.definition: Forcing a simulated device into a faulted state at runtime through the Web UI or the API.

fdp.definition: Foundry Discovery Protocol — Foundry/Brocade/Ruckus proprietary discovery.

firewall.definition: A device that enforces a security policy on traffic between zones.

fiveTuple.definition: A 5-tuple is the (protocol, source IP:port, destination IP:port) combination that uniquely identifies a TCP/UDP conversation.

fleet.definition: The collection of simulated devices in a network. Generate a fleet by choosing sites and device counts, then edit it in the wizard.

frame.definition: A Layer-2 packet — the unit Ethernet works in.

ftp.definition: File Transfer Protocol (RFC 959). NIAC implements only the banner / handshake, not real file transfer.

gateway.definition: Loose term for a router that connects different networks.

host.definition: A general-purpose end-system on the network — PC, server, IoT sensor.

http.definition: Hypertext Transfer Protocol. NIAC ships a minimal HTTP/1.1 responder with configurable endpoints.

icmp.definition: Internet Control Message Protocol — ping, traceroute, error reports.

icmpv6.definition: IPv6 version of ICMP. Includes Neighbor Discovery (ND), which replaces ARP for v6.

inform.definition: An SNMP "trap with ack" — the receiver must acknowledge receipt. Adds reliability.

ipcSocket.definition: Unix-domain socket used by the niac CLI to talk to the running daemon. Default path `/tmp/niac.sock`.

iperf3.definition: Network throughput-measurement protocol. NIAC speaks the control channel but does not perform real throughput tests.

jumboFrame.definition: Ethernet frame larger than the standard 1500-byte MTU — commonly 9000 bytes for storage networks.

lacp.definition: Link Aggregation Control Protocol (IEEE 802.1AX). Lets multiple physical links act as one logical link.

lease.definition: A DHCP-assigned IP plus duration. When the lease expires, the client must renew or release it.

librarySource.definition: starter files ship with NIAC, bundle files come from the published content bundle (niac content install), and user files were added or edited locally.

lldp.definition: Link Layer Discovery Protocol (IEEE 802.1AB). Vendor-neutral L2 discovery — the standard CDP replacement.

macAddress.definition: Media Access Control address. 48-bit unique-per-NIC identifier formatted aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff.

mdns.definition: Multicast DNS (RFC 6762). Used by Bonjour / Avahi for local-network service discovery.

mib.definition: Management Information Base. The schema describing what SNMP OIDs mean.

mtu.definition: Maximum Transmission Unit — the largest payload an interface can carry in one frame (default 1500 on Ethernet).

multicast.definition: Frames sent to a group address — one sender, many receivers. LLDP, CDP, STP, mDNS all use multicast.

netbios.definition: Legacy Windows name/service protocol (RFC 1001/1002). NIAC answers NBSTAT name queries.

nms.definition: Network Management System — a platform that polls / monitors devices (SolarWinds, LibreNMS, Zabbix, etc.).

offer.definition: Second DHCPv4 message: server responds to DISCOVER with a candidate lease.

oid.definition: An OID (object identifier) is the dotted-numeric address of a single value in an SNMP MIB tree, e.g. 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0 for sysDescr.

option82.definition: DHCP relay-agent information option. Lets a DHCP relay tell the server which port the client showed up on.

oui.definition: Organizationally Unique Identifier — the first 24 bits of a MAC, identifying the vendor.

pcap.definition: PCAP (packet capture) is the file format used to record and replay network traffic captured on the wire.

persona.definition: A device-type setting (router / switch / firewall / server / ap / iot / unknown) that applies sensible defaults.

poe.definition: Power over Ethernet (IEEE 802.3af/at/bt). Carries power to devices over the data cable.

portChannel.definition: A bundle of physical interfaces presented as one logical interface. Negotiated with LACP.

ptr.definition: DNS reverse-lookup record — IP to name.

rawSocket.definition: A socket that delivers L2 or L3 frames without OS protocol processing. NIAC needs raw sockets, which usually requires root.

rawSocketPrivilege.definition: The OS permission needed to open Layer-2 / Layer-3 raw sockets. Typically root, or CAP_NET_RAW on Linux.

recursiveResolver.definition: A DNS server that chases queries down through the hierarchy on the client’s behalf. NIAC is NOT one of these.

relayAgent.definition: A device that forwards DHCP requests across subnets (because DHCP DISCOVER is broadcast and broadcasts don’t cross routers).

request.definition: Third DHCPv4 message: client confirms it wants the offered lease.

router.definition: A device that forwards packets between networks at Layer 3.

scenarioPack.definition: A versioned starting point for a complete network, such as a hospital or campus. Select a pack in New Simulation to create an editable draft.

session.definition: One running simulation, started from a reviewed configuration on a selected interface. Stop the session to stop its simulated devices.

singleShotMode.definition: NIAC running one config to exit, foreground. Started with `niac daemon --once <iface> <config>`.

snmp.definition: Simple Network Management Protocol. Query and monitor device state via OIDs.

snmpv1.definition: Original SNMP (RFC 1157). Community-string auth, 32-bit counters, lossy traps.

snmpv2c.definition: SNMP v2 with community-string auth (RFC 3416/3418). Adds GetBulk and 64-bit counters.

snmpv3.definition: SNMP with USM-based authentication and optional encryption (RFC 3414/3826).

snmpWalk.definition: An SNMP walk is a saved sequence of OID/value pairs collected by walking a device's MIB tree with GetNext requests. NIAC replays these files to simulate a device's SNMP responses.

stpRSTPMSTP.definition: Spanning Tree Protocol family (IEEE 802.1D / 802.1w / 802.1s). Loop prevention via BPDU exchange.

switch.definition: A multi-port bridge — forwards Ethernet frames between ports based on MAC tables.

sysdescr.definition: SNMP sysDescr.0 — the device’s self-description string. Tools fingerprint vendors from this.

tcp.definition: Transmission Control Protocol — reliable, ordered transport. Underlies HTTP, FTP, etc.

template.definition: A built-in starter YAML config for a common device type. List with `niac template list`.

tlv.definition: Type-Length-Value. The encoding LLDP / CDP / DHCP options use — a tag, a length, then the data.

topologyConfig.definition: The YAML file that describes the simulated network: devices, protocols, VLANs.

trap.definition: An unsolicited SNMP message from a device to a configured receiver. Inform = trap with acknowledgement.

trunk.definition: A port carrying multiple VLANs, with each frame tagged using 802.1Q.

ttl.definition: Time-To-Live — a value that limits how long a packet or LLDP advertisement is considered valid.

udp.definition: User Datagram Protocol — lightweight, connectionless transport. Underlies DNS, SNMP, DHCP.

vlan.definition: Virtual LAN (IEEE 802.1Q). A way to partition one physical network into multiple broadcast domains.

walkFile.definition: A text file holding SNMP `OID = TYPE: VALUE` lines, used to drive NIAC’s SNMP agent for realistic responses.

walkProvenance.definition: Where a walk's content came from. "Captured" means an SNMP walk of a real device, put through the sanitizer. "Generated" means NIAC built it from a profile — it answers, but no device was ever measured for it.

overview.whatNiacDoesBody: NIAC (Network In A Can) simulates one or more network devices on a real host interface. It answers ARP, ICMP, LLDP, CDP, SNMP, DHCP, DNS, HTTP, FTP and other protocols so a discovery tool, NMS, or monitoring platform sees the simulated devices as if they were physical hardware. Use it for tooling validation, training labs, and reproducer environments without standing up real gear.

block0.text: The daemon emits an alert webhook when the total packet count crosses the configured threshold. Useful for catching runaway traffic from a misconfigured device persona.

block2.text: Outbound webhook destinations are gated by an SSRF defence: raw private / loopback / link-local IPs are rejected, and if the daemon was started with `--webhook-allowed-host`, only those hostnames are allowed. Set the allowlist in production rather than relying on the implicit IP filter — see [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/MustardSeedNetworks/niac-go/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

block4.text: Leave the threshold blank or set it to 0 to disable packet alerts entirely.
